core_meaning.short_meaning: Beloved love, drops of dew; companion al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir (Dhu al-Ra'y).
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Hubab (حُبَاب) is an authentic Arabic masculine given name meaning 'beloved affection', 'clear drops of morning dew', or 'the glistening surface of water'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir al-Ansari, known as 'Dhu al-Ra'y' (The Man of Sound Counsel) whose strategic military counsel at the Battle of Badr was embraced by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Derived from ḥabb / ḥubb, signifying sweet affection, radiant dew on desert petals, or the crest of flowing water.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root ḥ-b-b is the foundation of love and affection in Arabic. Al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir was a veteran chieftain of the Khazraj. At the Battle of Badr, he politely inquired of the Prophet ﷺ whether the encampment location was divine revelation or human strategy. When told it was human strategy, Hubab suggested encamping at the closest well to the enemy and stopping up the rest, which the Prophet ﷺ praised and implemented immediately.
